common_name: Seaside Serenade Cape Cod Hydrangea (Reblooming Blue-to-Pink Mophead Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Cape Cod is a member of the Seaside Serenade series of reblooming bigleaf hydrangeas bred for a tidy habit and abundant, full mophead clusters over a long season.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, giving it morning sun with afternoon shade in hot climates. Cape Cod blooms on both old and new wood, so it recovers and reblooms through summer even if a late frost damages the previous season's buds. Flower color follows soil pH, shifting toward blue in acidic soil and pink in neutral to alkaline soil, and can be nudged with soil amendments or hydrangea colorant products. Keep the root zone evenly moist and mulched, and limit pruning to a light shaping right after the first flush to preserve old-wood buds for later blooms.

common_name: Seaside Serenade Bar Harbor Hydrangea (Compact Reblooming Mophead Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Bar Harbor is one of the more compact members of the Seaside Serenade series, keeping a dense, rounded form well suited to smaller foundation beds and large containers.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, sheltering it from harsh afternoon sun in warm regions. Bar Harbor sets flower buds on both old and new stems, giving it a dependable rebloom through the season even after winter injury to older wood, and its dwarfer, tighter habit makes it easier to tuck into smaller borders or containers than full-sized bigleaf hydrangeas. Bloom color moves from blue-purple in acidic soil to rosy pink in neutral to alkaline soil. Water deeply during dry stretches, mulch to buffer soil temperature, and prune only lightly immediately after the first bloom flush.

common_name: Tuff Stuff Ah-Ha Hydrangea (Bold-Blue Reblooming Mountain Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Ah-Ha is a Tuff Stuff series mountain hydrangea selected for larger, more saturated lacecap flowers than the original Tuff Stuff.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, protecting it from intense afternoon sun in hot climates. Ah-Ha flowers on both old and new wood, so it keeps producing its bold, deeply colored lacecap blooms through summer even when a hard late freeze damages the prior year's buds. As with other mountain hydrangeas, flower color intensifies toward blue in acidic soil and shifts toward pink-purple in neutral to alkaline soil, and the compact, sturdy stems hold up well without staking. Water regularly through dry spells, mulch to keep roots cool, and prune lightly right after the first flush rather than in fall or winter.

common_name: Nuccio's Cameo Camellia (Soft Pink Formal Double Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; Nuccio's Cameo, from California's Nuccio's Nurseries, joins the breeder's long line of exhibition-quality camellia introductions.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, shielded from harsh afternoon sun. Nuccio's Cameo produces soft, clear pink formal double flowers with tightly imbricated petals arranged in neat concentric rows, a refined show form typical of the Nuccio's Nurseries breeding line. The upright evergreen shrub blooms in mid to late season and holds its flower shape well both in the garden and as a cut bloom for exhibition. Maintain an acidic, evenly moist root zone with a heavy pine bark or pine straw mulch, and prune only to remove dead or crossing wood right after flowering.

common_name: Spring Sonnet Camellia (Deep Rose-Pink Peony-Form Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; Spring Sonnet is a widely grown show and landscape camellia valued for its full, high-centered peony-form blooms.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, sheltered from strong afternoon sun. Spring Sonnet bears large, deep rose-pink flowers with a full peony-to-anemone form packed with ruffled petaloids, opening over a long midseason-to-late bloom window on a vigorous, upright evergreen shrub. The dense flower form and rich color make it a popular choice for both garden display and cut-flower use. Keep the soil consistently moist and acidic with a generous pine bark or pine straw mulch, and prune lightly right after flowering to shape and remove crossing growth.
